findings.description: A dropped task still raises its top-rung need: `topRungFailure` in src/core/dashboard.service.ts only checks the task row exists, and the dashboard reads tasks via `listTasks` (which includes dropped rows), so after `pup plan drop` the "re-plan or pup launch" need never clears.
findings.body:
**A dropped task still raises its top-rung need.**

`dropTask` now marks a task with killed sessions as dropped, but on the dashboard only `listBacklogTasks` reads `dropped_at`. `buildDashboardSnapshot` builds its task map from `listTasks`, which still returns dropped rows (ADR 0147 says so on purpose). `topRungFailure` only checks that the task row exists:

```ts
if (row.state !== 'killed' || !task) return undefined;
```
https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/84e8a714672ee740d499131194d8345c22389801/src/core/dashboard.service.ts#L265-L280

Its doc limits it to "the newest of a task still in the store". Before this PR that meant the same as "back in the backlog" for a killed-only task. Now it doesn't.

**Trigger:** a task's newest session is killed after it fails on the top rung, so `needsYou` shows `top rung: …` with the answer `re-plan t-x, or pup launch t-x --model … --effort …`. The operator re-plans it: `pup plan drop t-x` now succeeds (https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/84e8a714672ee740d499131194d8345c22389801/src/core/session.repository.ts#L315-L317), then `pup plan add …`. The `top-rung` need for t-x stays in `pup status`, the terminal status line, `fleetSummary` and the web dashboard, and nothing can clear it. `needsYou` has no backlog check, and ADR 0147's Ceilings section doesn't list this.

**Fix:** return `undefined` for a dropped task in `topRungFailure`. Update its doc and the `topReached` doc in `dashboard.types.ts` to match, and add a dashboard test where the task is dropped after a top-rung kill.

findings.description: No test exercises the sanitizing half of the drop fix: both new CLI tests use plain ids (`t-s1`, `s1`), so removing any `sanitizeReason` call in the `plan drop` branch (src/cli/index.ts:1052, 1056, 1059) leaves every test green. Add a claimed-drop case whose session id holds a control character and assert that the refusal shows it sanitized.
